text:
jess: Heads up — ran into duplicate DB inserts in the onboarding sample when a streaming generation hit a 429 during token rotation. Pretty sure its a replay/idempotency gap across SDK retries.

lee: ouch. is this the same as the earlier 429 replay issues or something new?

jess: Related but different. Flow: client starts streaming request -> mid-stream auth refresh triggers a retry -> the retry gets a 429 -> SDK issues a retry after backoff but the apps webhook receives both the partial in-progress event and the retried completion payload which contains the same logical event but we didn't attach any dedupe id.

rob: do you have the minimal repro? can we simulate in e2e?

jess: yes repro harness attached to my branch. Logs:```
2024-11-03T11:22:10Z INFO start req=abc123
2024-11-03T11:22:10Z INFO auth:rotating token
2024-11-03T11:22:11Z WARN http 429 req=abc123
2024-11-03T11:22:11Z INFO retrying req=abc123 backoff=120ms jittered
2024-11-03T11:22:11Z INFO webhook POST /events id=evt-789 status=200
2024-11-03T11:22:12Z INFO webhook POST /events id=evt-789 status=200 (duplicate)
```

lee: Hmm. Two axes: 1) backoff/jitter behavior on 429 (we should use decorrelated jitter) 2) idempotency across resume/retries (SDK should carry a stable replay id).

rob: SDK parity question: do Node/Python/Go SDKs all preserve headers across internal resume/retry logic today? I thought Go had a slightly different streaming implementation.

anna: We do not consistently preserve app-level custom headers for internal resume requests. Some SDKs re-create the HTTP request which drops ephemeral headers. That's probably the root cause.

jess: Proposed plan: - SDK change: generate an ephemeral X-Redwood-Replay header at request start and guarantee it is preserved for all retry/resume attempts. Also expose sdkContext.replay_id to apps. - Retry policy: 429 backoff should be decorrelated jitter (per Erlang/Exponential backoff best practices) with a max cap and a short-circuit for streaming resume attempts (try resume-first before full retry). - Sampleapp: update examples to echo `X-Redwood-Replay` into their outgoing side-effecting POSTs as `X-Idempotency-Key` to help consumer dedupe.

lee: I like preserve-in-sdk as the default for DX, but we should make it opt-out via `preserveReplayId: false` config for advanced users. Default true in quickstarts.

rob: Parity work items: Node + Python already have a single request lifecycle hook, but Go's streaming client spawns goroutines that reconstruct outbound requests. We'll need a small refactor to pass a request-scoped metadata struct rather than re-computing headers.

jess: Example snippets for docs:
Node sampleapp snippet:```js
// handler receives sdkContext with replayId
const replay = req.sdkContext?.replayId || uuid();
await fetch(process.env.CONSUMER_URL, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'X-Idempotency-Key': replay, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ event, replay })
});
```
Python SDK consumer example:```py
replay = request.sdk_context.get('replay_id') or uuid4().hex
requests.post(os.environ['CONSUMER_URL'], headers={'X-Idempotency-Key': replay}, json={'event': event, 'replay': replay})
```

anna: Tests: add an e2e that forces token rotation mid-stream + instrumented 429 on retry and assert webhook receiver sees exactly one idempotent event (same idempotency key). Also unit tests for header preservation across retry/resume cycles.

ci-bot: ci: e2e flake detected on sampleapp webhook tests. See job https://ci.example.com/8845

lee: Telemetry: emit `sdk.replay_id.preserved` boolean and `sdk.replay_id.generated` when we create one. This helps measure adoption and any downstream impact.

rob: One gotcha: some customers route headers through proxies that strip unknown headers. Maybe we should use `X-Redwood-Replay` internally and encourage apps to mirror it into their `X-Idempotency-Key` when talking to third-party consumers. Docs note required.

jess: Agreed. We'll have the SDK auto-add `X-Redwood-Replay` for internal calls, expose replayId on ctx, and add a sample helper to mirror into consumer headers.

anna: Timeline: I'll open two PRs: 1) SDK header preservation + telemetry (Node, Python, Go) 2) sampleapp updates + e2e harness. Hoping for code review next week.

lee: Add a short doc in devex quickstart: "Handling duplicate side-effects during onboarding" with a small diagram.

jess: Thanks folks. I'll link PRs here when ready and add the flaky e2e case to CI so we don't regress. :thumbsup:

rob: If you want, I can take the Go refactor. Its the tightest change.

jess: Please do, that'd be great.
